thread:
maya (support): FYI we have a high-severity from Acme about JSON outputs being 'merged' across requests when they enable batching + prefix cache. Customer says their structured outputs are intermittently invalid.
acme-infra (customer): Repro steps: 1) POST /v1/generate with json_mode=true & cache_prefix=true, 2) send 40 concurrent requests with short prompts, 3) ~6% of responses return two JSON objects concatenated or fields from another request mixed in. We see parse errors in downstream pipeline.
maya (support): Thanks. Can you paste an example response?
acme-infra (customer): Example (sanitized):
```
{"id":"req-102","items":[{"name":"widget","qty":3}],"meta":{"user":"u123"}}{"id":"req-107","items":[{"name":"gadget","qty":1}],"meta":{"user":"u456"}}
```
We see two top-level JSON objects stuck together. Sometimes keys are interleaved, like "items":[{...}, { ...from other req... }].
oliver (eng-runtime): Hmm that looks like stream boundary / KV cache bleed. Do you have streaming=true on these calls?
acme-infra (customer): Yes, streaming=true to keep latency low. We also use the prefix cache to reuse prompt tokens.
jamal (sre): @oliver :eyes: can you check batch scheduler logs? This smells like a race where the batching worker reuses the same output buffer before previous request's stream markers cleared.
oliver (eng-runtime): Will dig in. Quick hypothesis: when prefix cache returns a cached response buffer, and streaming frames are interleaved with new generation frames, the emitter might not always insert the JSON separator we expect. Also the prefix cache stores partial KV states that could map to different request ids if eviction coincides with a batch boundary.
maya (support): Customer reports it's blocking production. They tried toggling batching_size=1 and problem disappeared.
oliver (eng-runtime): Important repro detail - batching_size>1 + prefix_cache=true + streaming=true + structured_output=json_schema. That combination seems to trigger it. Thanks for the repro.
jamal (sre): I pulled the pod logs for the timeframe they gave. See these snippets: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:22:03Z] batch_worker[pid=82] start batch id=bb-77 reqs=24
[2026-03-15T14:22:03Z] cache.lookup prefix=acct/u123/17 -> hit
[2026-03-15T14:22:03Z] emitter:req-102 stream_frame seq=8 payload=\"...\\n\"
[2026-03-15T14:22:03Z] cache.evict prefix=acct/u123/17 reason=mempressure
[2026-03-15T14:22:03Z] emitter:req-107 stream_frame seq=1 payload=\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"req-107\\\",...\"
[2026-03-15T14:22:03Z] emitter:req-102 stream_frame seq=9 payload=\"}\n```
jamal (sre): You can see eviction happened mid-batch, and frames for req-107 started being emitted while req-102 hadn't finished flush. If the flush marker isn't enforced, the consumer sees concatenated objects.
oliver (eng-runtime): This matches a bug I filed earlier about output buffer tagging. Root cause: output buffers are pooled and reused without clearing the 'last_frame_emitted' sentinel when a cached prefix is replayed into a new stream. For cached prefixes we treated them as read-only and skipped some lifecycle steps; when eviction occurs concurrently, we can end up with overlapping frame writes.
maya (support): Customer asked for workaround ASAP — what can we advise?
oliver (eng-runtime): Short term: tell them to set batching_size=1 OR disable prefix_cache for JSON-streaming endpoints. Also they can set streaming=false to receive a single well-formed JSON response (higher latency). I'll prepare an internal flag to force per-request buffer isolation as a hotfix.
jamal (sre): Also recommend rate-limiting concurrent streams per connection as a mitigation.
oncall-bot: @jamal you're on call for eng-sre. Incident created: INC-2026-1387 (json-streaming-cache-race)
jamal (sre): I'll escalate to prod oncall. @oliver can you produce a minimal failing unit test for the batch runner and a loggable repro harness? If we have deterministic test, we can patch quickly.
oliver (eng-runtime): Yes, I'll add a harness that simulates concurrent cache hit + eviction during batch flush and include asserts for buffer ownership and final separators. ETA 6h.
maya (support): I'll send the customer the mitigation steps and offer to run them through a staging repro. We should also offer credits if they took production downtime.
acme-infra (customer): Appreciate the quick response. They accepted disabling prefix cache as a short-term fix. Asking for ETA on permanent fix.
oliver (eng-runtime): Plan: 1) Add per-request buffer tagging + enforce end-of-stream sentinel when emitting cached prefixes (hotfix) — target: next patch release (canary within 8h). 2) Add an integration test for streaming+prefix_cache+batches. 3) In follow-up, consider stronger invariants: never reuse output buffers across different request ids and add metrics for 'interleaved_frames' detection.
jamal (sre): I'll monitor canary and watch for increased memory usage due to buffer isolation. If mem goes up, we'll throttle prefix cache.
maya (support): Thanks team. I'll update the customer and mark the thread as escalated. :thumbsup:
oliver (eng-runtime): quick note for postmortem: add a warning to docs that structured output + streaming + prefix cache is currently sensitive until we land the fix.
maya (support): Filed support ticket and billing credit request: TCK-4519.
acme-infra (customer): Once hotfix lands, we'll re-enable prefix cache and run our 10k-concurrent test. Please ping when canary completes.
maya (support): Pinged again.
jamal (sre): Canary deployed to 10% at 2026-03-15T22:40Z by deploy-bot. Monitoring traces.
oncall-bot: Canary alert: 5xx spike in region-us-east for ab test -> rollback initiated.
jamal (sre): Rolled back. The hotfix caused an unexpected mem increase; working with oliver to reduce buffer overhead.
oliver (eng-runtime): Revised fix is up — uses zero-copy tag metadata instead of full buffer duplication. Canary 10% now, no mem spike.
jamal (sre): No JSON interleaving observed in canary logs for 24h window.
maya (support): Customer notified; they will re-test. Closing escalation if they confirm.
acme-infra (customer): Confirmed after re-test: no more merged JSON outputs. Thanks team.
maya (support): Closing thread.
